chunks: And the trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon away, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown a second time, and suddenly they will be standing, looking on.

key_terms.أُخْرَىٰ: A second time (referring to the second blowing of the trumpet)
key_terms.الصُّور: The Trumpet blown by the angel Israfil to signal major eschatological events
key_terms.صَعِقَ: To swoon, faint, or fall into a deep death-like sleep
key_terms.قِيَامٌ: Standing up (from their graves or states of unconsciousness)

ai.seo_question: What happens when the Trumpet is blown for the second time on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the universal scope of the Resurrection, where the first blow induces a state of death or fainting for all creation except those preserved by divine will, such as the Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt. The second blow signifies the immediate awakening for judgment, emphasizing the suddenness and totality of the Day of Reckoning as described in the Quranic narrative.
